pl-l4d44c3-d1e112.summary: Continues Augustine on the saints' bodies: they will rise without any vice or deformity, as without corruption, burden, or difficulty, with as much ease as happiness; so they are called spiritual, though they will surely be bodies, not spirits.

pl-l4d44c3-d1e118.summary: Concludes that all rising will have one age, the youthful age each had or would have had if he died earlier.

pl-l4d44c3-d1e121.summary: States that nothing of the substance from which man's flesh is created will perish, but by gathering all its scattered particles the body's natural substance will be restored (sentence continues).
claims: All the body's scattered matter is regathered.

pl-l4d44c3-d1e124.summary: Completes: and the saints' bodies will rise without any vice, shining like the sun, all deformities they had here removed.
claims: The saints rise shining, without deformity.

pl-l4d44c3.summary: This applies to the saints' bodies, which will rise without vice, deformity, corruption, burden, or difficulty, with ease matching their happiness; they are called spiritual though they remain bodies. So all will rise at the youthful age they had or would have had; nothing of their substance will perish, its scattered particles being gathered; and the saints' bodies will rise shining like the sun, their deformities removed.
claims: The saints' bodies rise without defect or burden.
The saints rise shining, their deformities removed.
